experiment: C&W-L2 attacker, on-device (Raspberry Pi 5, aarch64 A76), real d=42 surrogate
method: shadow/run_cw_real.py + shadow/cw_attack.py. Carlini-Wagner L2 (untargeted, binary sigmoid), tanh-space parametrization, Adam, iters=100, binary-search over c in {1,4,16}, initial_c=1, lr=0.01. Attack objective BCE to natural label; success = defended prediction flips. Real UNSW-NB15 benign samples, W=10, gamma=1.984, tau=0.75, n=200, seed 42.

attacker_models.naive: rotation theta and basis detached from gradient (fixed view of defense)
attacker_models.adaptive: gradients flow through entire defense incl. rotation angle and coupled basis

c_and_w_vs_pgd_contrast.fixed_pca2_basis: Adaptive == naive (0.610 vs 0.610). Adaptive attacker gains NO advantage over naive on the deployed basis. Consistent with PGD gate.
c_and_w_vs_pgd_contrast.attacker_coupled_basis: Adaptive (0.295) LOWER than naive (0.475) — the OPPOSITE of PGD (where adaptive ~0.94 beat naive ~0.41). Mechanistic cause: for coupled basis, adaptive gradient flows through a basis that moves with the attacker's own point (vulnerable_basis(x_t)), making the objective strongly non-stationary for Adam-based C&W; PGD's sign dynamics are less affected. This is a real attack-methodology contrast, reported honestly, NOT relabeled as a MIDAS robustness win.
c_and_w_vs_pgd_contrast.reproducibility: n=60 smoke reproduced identically on dev box and Pi (naive/coupled 0.750, adaptive/coupled 0.533, fixed 0.633/0.633). n=200 Pi run: coupled naive 0.475 / adaptive 0.295; fixed 0.610/0.610.
